subject: cdf incompatibilities while reloading previously analysed data

messages.subject: cdf incompatibilities while reloading previously analysed data
parts:
Dear all,


I am trying to reload previously analysed data with :
> AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name="10thserie,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY",cdf=cdf,paths="plmData")
forcing the path to plmData, and using the same cdf than used during
the analysis.

However, I catch an exception complaining that the current cdf is
different from the one used during the analysis. It seems the number
of cells do not match.
Have you experienced such problem before ? Or am I just doing
something wrong ?

Thanks a lot for your help,
BW,
Armand

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] cdf incompatibilities while reloading previously analysed data
parts:
On Wed, Oct 29, 2008 at 2:39 AM, armand.v...@gmail.com
<armand....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear all,
>
>
> I am trying to reload previously analysed data with :
>> AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name="10thserie,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY",cdf=cdf,paths="plmData")
> forcing the path to plmData, and using the same cdf than used during
> the analysis.

What I still recommend is to just rerun the complete script from
start. The package will detect which steps are already processed and
skip them. The overhead for doing this that it takes a little while
for aroma.affymetrix to verify that a step is actually complete,
before moving to the next. I use this more or less all the time.

At the end, I'll show how to do what you are trying to do:

>
> However, I catch an exception complaining that the current cdf is
> different from the one used during the analysis. It seems the number
> of cells do not match.

Yes, this is because the CEL set you are trying to "load" consists of
so called chip-effect CEL files, which has less cells ("probes") and
these cells are mapped according to a so called monocell CDF. There is
a bit on monocell CDFs on Page 'Setting up annotation files':

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/setup

In your case you are trying to use the original CDF, but you really
need the monocell CDF, e.g.

Filename: GenomeWideSNP_5,Full,r2.cdf
Filesize: 249.46MB
Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_5,Full,r2
RAM: 0.00MB
File format: v4 (binary; XDA)
Dimension: 2166x2166
Number of cells: 4691556
Number of units: 920928
Cells per unit: 5.09
Number of QC units: 6

Dimension: 1201x1201
Number of cells: 1442401
Number of units: 920928
Cells per unit: 1.57

> Have you experienced such problem before ? Or am I just doing
> something wrong ?

Next: "If you find yourself specifying paths or full pathname in your main
aroma.affymetrix scripts, you are doing something wrong. The package
is design to work without having to specify paths. A rule of thumb is
that you should be able to move any aroma.affymetrix script to another
computer system and run it without having to change anything." [thread
'How do you analyze Gene ST Data?', Oct 21, 2008].

To "load" an existing chip-effect set, do:

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("GenomeWideSNP_5", tags="Full,r2");
cdfM <- getMonocellCdf(cdf);
dataSet <- "10thserie";
tags <- "ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY";
cesN <- CnChipEffectSet$byName(dataSet, tags=tags, cdf=cdfM,
mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE);

If you do not explicitly specify the arguments 'mergeStrands' and
'combineAlleles', these has to be inferred from the data itself, which
will take some time. To avoid this overhead, specify it explicitly.
It is important that you use the same value as when you fitted the
PLM.

Note that you have to specify class 'CnChipEffectSet', because that is
the class of the chip-effect set you are loading. It is true that
this is a subset of AffymetrixCelSet, but if you use the latter (as
you did), you will get an object that is of that class.

FYI, use byName() instead of deprecated alias fromName(). For my
information (so I can correct it), is there documentation online that
still use fromName()? Where did you learn about this?

Hope this helps

Henrik
